meta.title: Infinite Canvas
meta.description: A pannable, zoomable node canvas — drag to pan, wheel to zoom, shift-drag to rubber-band select, drag nodes individually or as a group. The engine writes transforms straight to the DOM during gestures, so panning and dragging stay smooth regardless of node count.
features: Pan, zoom, and rubber-band select out of the box
Single and multi-node dragging, with optional grid snapping
Three pan triggers: plain drag, space+drag, or middle-mouse
zoomToFit and centerOn for programmatic camera control
Gesture-critical updates write to the DOM directly — React re-renders only on commit

blocks.content: An infinite canvas looks like a solved problem until you build one. Pan has to feel instant, which rules out re-rendering React on every pointermove. Zoom has to zoom toward the cursor, not the origin, which means converting screen coordinates to canvas coordinates before and after every scale change. Selection needs both click-to-select and shift-drag rubber-banding, and both need to agree with whatever's mid-drag. None of it can block the frame.

CanvasRoot owns a single engine instance that holds the viewport, the node list, and the current gesture. Pan and node-drag write directly to the DOM through cached element refs and skip React entirely while the gesture is in progress; the engine only calls back into React once a gesture ends, to commit the final state. Selection boxes render through React since they're a lightweight, short-lived overlay — see Performance model for the full breakdown.

blocks.title: Category still forming
blocks.content: Canvas is filed under "canvas-editor" for now — update this if it should sit under a different category once the docs taxonomy for node/editor systems is finalized.
Drag empty space to pan, scroll to zoom toward the cursor, shift-drag to rubber-band select, drag a node (or a multi-selection) to move it. Positions snap to the grid.
Pass defaultNodes and a renderNode function to CanvasRoot. The engine handles position, selection, and drag — renderNode only returns what goes inside each node's box.

Node mutations go through useCanvas and are immutable, matching the convention used by Sortable and Palette Editor — each call returns a new node array rather than mutating in place. Pass onChange to CanvasRoot to persist the node list wherever it needs to live.

Clicking a node selects it and starts a drag in the same gesture. Shift-click adds to the current selection. Dragging empty space with the default pan trigger rubber-bands a selection box; the exact gesture that triggers rubber-banding vs. panning depends on config.panTrigger — see Pan trigger modes.

Panning and zooming work out of the box from pointer and wheel input. zoomToFit and centerOn give you programmatic control — useful for a "fit to screen" toolbar button or focusing a node after it's created or searched for.

blocks.title: Zoom follows the cursor
blocks.content: Wheel-triggered zoom in CanvasViewport passes the pointer position to zoomTo as the zoom origin, so the point under the cursor stays fixed while the rest of the canvas scales around it. Call zoomTo without an origin for a plain zoom around the current view center.
config.panTrigger decides which gesture pans the canvas and which one rubber-band selects. Pick the mode that matches the rest of your app's interaction model.

rows.description: Default. Plain drag on empty space pans; shift+drag rubber-bands a selection.

blocks.content: Pass children to CanvasRoot instead of renderNode to compose your own viewport — for example to add a zoom control overlay, a minimap, or a toolbar anchored inside the same context.

Two gestures are perf-sensitive enough to bypass React entirely while in progress: panning and node dragging. Both write a CSS transform directly to a cached DOM element on every pointermove, and only call the engine's notify() once the gesture ends — at which point React re-renders with the committed viewport or node positions. Rubber-band selection notifies on every move instead, since it's a short-lived, lower-frequency gesture and the visual is a single lightweight overlay div rather than a scene with potentially hundreds of nodes.

blocks.title: Reading state mid-drag
blocks.content: Because pan and node-drag skip notify(), useCanvas's viewport and nodes values won't reflect a drag in progress — they update once the gesture ends. If you need live position data during a drag (e.g. for a coordinates readout), read engine.getViewport() / engine.getNodes() directly rather than the hook's snapshot.

items.q: Can nodes contain interactive content, like inputs or buttons?
items.a: Yes. renderNode returns arbitrary React content. CanvasNodeView calls stopPropagation on pointerdown so clicks inside a node don't trigger a canvas pan or rubber-band select; interactive elements inside your node content behave normally.

items.q: How do I lock a node in place?
items.a: Set locked: true on the node. CanvasNodeView skips drag entirely for locked nodes and shows a default cursor instead of the grab cursor.
No — updateNodeDrag divides the raw pointer delta by the current zoom level before applying it, so a node tracks the cursor 1:1 in canvas space regardless of zoom.
